title: U.S. House · Missouri's 2nd District
area: Western St. Louis County and St. Charles County suburbs, including Chesterfield, Ballwin, Wildwood and St. Charles.

context.text: Incumbent Ann Wagner won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Matthew Grant, Peter Pfeifer, Elizabeth Sparks-Holmes and Brandon Wilkinson. Frederick Wellman won the Democratic primary over Timothy D. Bilash and Joan VonDras. Brandon Daugherty advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Ann Wagner

summary.text: Ann Wagner is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 2nd District, first elected in 2012. A former Missouri Republican Party chair, Republican National Committee co-chair and U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg, she serves on the House Financial Services and Intelligence committees, where she chairs the Financial Services Subcommittee on Capital Markets.

background.text: Born September 13, 1962, in St. Louis; according to her House biography, she grew up working in her parents' retail carpet store in Manchester, Missouri, and attended Cor Jesu Academy.
Graduated from the University of Missouri-Columbia in 1984 with a degree in business administration, specializing in logistics.
Worked in management for Hallmark Cards in Kansas City and Ralston Purina in St. Louis.

Entered Republican politics in 1990, serving nine years as a Lafayette Township committeewoman; served as the first woman to chair the Missouri Republican Party (1999-2005) and as co-chair of the Republican National Committee (2001-2005).
Served as U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg from 2005 to 2009, after nomination by President George W. Bush and Senate confirmation.
Chaired Roy Blunt's 2010 U.S. Senate campaign before running for Congress herself.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 with more than 60% of the vote and took office in January 2013; her House biography says her freshman and sophomore classes chose her as their representative on the Elected Leadership Committee.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, where she chairs the Subcommittee on Capital Markets, and on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

Authored the Retail Investor Protection Act and anti-trafficking legislation including the SAVE Act and the Allow States and Victims to Fight Online Sex Trafficking Act (FOSTA), which became law in April 2018.
According to her House biography, lives in Ballwin with her husband, Ray, and they have three children.

priorities.text: Lists budget and spending, the economy and jobs, defense and national security, energy, and veterans issues among her legislative priorities.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. should fully cultivate domestic oil resources by ending drilling moratoriums and increasing onshore and offshore production rather than relying on oil imports.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Financial Services, where she chairs the Subcommittee on Capital Markets, and on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, chairing its Open Source Intelligence Subcommittee.

candidates.name: Frederick Wellman

summary.text: Frederick (Fred) Wellman is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 2nd District. A West Point graduate and Army helicopter pilot who served more than 20 years, he later founded a communications firm for veterans and served as a senior advisor and executive director of the Lincoln Project. He is campaigning on affordability, healthcare and retirement security.

background.text: Grew up in Kirkwood, Missouri, and graduated from Kirkwood High School.
Graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and earned a master's degree from Harvard's Kennedy School (2007).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1987 to 2010 as a helicopter pilot and officer, with multiple deployments to Iraq, and earned his Ranger tab; he describes himself as a third-generation military veteran.
After retiring from the Army, founded ScoutComms, a firm that he says invested in veterans and military families, and worked as an advocate and consultant.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, helped lead a team of Special Operations medical veterans that built and ran a field hospital in New York City.
Later served as Senior Advisor and Executive Director of the Lincoln Project.

Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for Missouri's 2nd District with 45.8% of the vote, ahead of Joan VonDras (43.0%) and Timothy Bilash (11.1%); he lives in Wildwood, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

priorities.text: Affordability: says families face rising costs for housing, healthcare, childcare and groceries while wages stay flat, and calls for lowering costs and expanding good-paying jobs.
Healthcare: supports a public option and allowing people to buy into Medicare before age 65 to increase competition and lower premiums.
Retirement security: wants to protect Social Security and Medicare and defend pensions.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to affordable healthcare through a public option and allowing Missourians to buy into Medicare before turning 65.
Calls for immediately raising the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: We must immediately raise the federal minimum wage

positions.summary: Says Congress must exercise its constitutional war powers and that the Iran conflict lacks congressional authorization.
positions.quote: Congress must exercise its constitutional war powers, demand clear objectives and accountability, and pursue serious diplomacy.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign website.

candidates.name: Brandon Daugherty
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Brandon Daugherty is the Libertarian Party nominee for Missouri's 2nd District. He works in hospitality management and is a local Libertarian Party officer who ran for the same seat in 2024; his 2024 Ballotpedia survey describes support for individual liberties, lower taxes and a non-interventionist foreign policy.

background.text: Born in Columbia, Missouri; says he grew up in rural Warren County and now lives in O'Fallon.
Earned an associate degree from St. Charles Community College in 2020.
Works in hospitality management.
Has been affiliated with the St. Charles County Libertarian Party and described himself as its vice chair in his 2024 Ballotpedia survey.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Missouri's 2nd District in 2024, receiving about 2.1% of the vote behind Ann Wagner and Ray Hartmann; he advanced from the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary.

priorities.text: Free markets, limited government and a non-interventionist foreign policy.
priorities.quote: I support free markets, limited government, and a non-interventionist foreign policy, emphasizing personal freedom and voluntary interactions for economic and societal prosperity.

priorities.text: Bring U.S. troops home from overseas.
priorities.quote: My vision for America includes bringing all troops home from overseas.

priorities.text: Reduce regulation and shrink or eliminate federal agencies.
priorities.quote: I will advocate for less government regulations and fight to shrink or eliminate as many three letter agencies as possible.

positions.summary: Pledged on his 2024 campaign website not to vote for any legislation that restricts gun ownership for law-abiding Americans.
positions.quote: I promise not to vote for or endorse ANY legislation that restricts gun ownership for law-abiding Americans.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities come from his 2024 campaign website as reproduced on Ballotpedia; he has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (he did in 2024) and no current campaign website was found. Statements are dated 2024. No stated position found on abortion, taxes on high earners, health coverage or most other guide issues.

statements.quote: I will lead the charge on reforming immigration to bring back Ellis Island standards with increased points of entry and immediate access to green cards once a background check is cleared.
statements.context: From his 2024 campaign website, as reproduced on Ballotpedia
